_source.system: v1 live, smartcityos.io Finance tab, City of Bastrop TX
_source.caveat: Every figure here is READ OFF A COMPRESSED SCREENSHOT. Digits are legible at the magnitudes that matter and the defects below survive any plausible OCR error, but no figure here is a reading of the source system. Before any of this reaches a customer artefact it is verified against OpenGov and MyGov directly. Figures are cited by capture page.
_source.whyItExists: The v2 Finance lens is designed against this capture the way the Development services lens was designed against its own. The capture is not a style reference. It is the evidence for what v2 must refuse to do.

connectedSource.name: OpenGov ERP API
connectedSource.headerVerbatim: CONNECTED  OpenGov ERP API  6 budgets - 3247 accounts - 2247 line items
connectedSource.note: This is the ONE of four required sources v1 genuinely reads. The other three are fabricated, corrupted, or absent, and that is the whole finding.

observations: The fifteen rows sum to roughly $128M against a stated total budget of $69.6M. Even allowing generous OCR error the sum is close to double the total, so the panel is either summing across funds that are not all in this budget, or double counting CIP against operating, or mixing appropriation with fund balance. It is presented with no counting rule.
Two rows name the same tax: Hotel Occupancy Fund and Hotel Occupancy Tax. That may be a legitimate fund-versus-revenue-account distinction and the panel does not say which.
Fund 701 is rendered by number. The fund has no name on this screen.

departmentAnalyzer.cautionVerbatim: Expense figures are estimated from annual budget totals - actual expenditure data is not available for this department.
departmentAnalyzer.insightVerbatim: Expense figures for Non-Departmental are estimated based on 100% FY elapsed. Actual expenditure data is not currently available from BMP or Transparency sources.
departmentAnalyzer.alarmVerbatim: Non-Departmental is approaching budget cap at 100% - only $0 remaining.
departmentAnalyzer.finding: Ten rows, ten identical Budget and Actual Spent pairs, 100% burn on every one. Actual Spent is the Budget column copied. The product states this in a caution banner on this one sub-tab and then consumes the figures as measured everywhere else, including an alarm derived from the fabricated equality.

findings: A collection rate of 157% is not a possible state. Collected cannot exceed charged. It is rendered in green with a success mark.

The surplus is traceable to one partition: Unassigned collected $450.9M against $170.9M charged, page 8. That single row is roughly $280M of unattributed surplus and it is the second largest line in the breakdown.

The magnitudes are impossible for this city. $664.7M collected against a total city operating budget of $69.6M is nine and a half times the whole budget, in permit fees. Building Department alone is $244.1M across 1,055 permits, or about $231,000 per permit.
The permit counts do not tie. The header says 1,877 permits. The department rows sum to 3,138 on page 25 and 4,052 on page 8.
The two pages disagree with each other. Building Department is 1,055 permits on page 25 and 1,970 on page 8, with different totals to match.
Outstanding balance is $0 on the header while the page-8 rows carry $918,547.40 outstanding on Building alone.

SPENT YTD $74.6M is revenue, not spend. Page 2 labels the same figure REVENUE against EXPENSES $69.6M, and the page-1 insight text agrees: "Current spending projects $64.6M annual expenditure on $74.6M budgeted revenue." A mislabeled field is feeding the most prominent card on the lens, and it renders as spending over budget with a positive variance.
DEPARTMENTS ON TRACK reads 1/1 while the same product lists 29 departments. The denominator is revenue-bearing departments and the card does not say so.

scenarioModeler.liveDataSources: 3/3 connected: OpenGov (Budget & Finance), Samsara (Fleet), Power BI (CIP Projects)
scenarioModeler.exampleSummary: This scenario costs an additional $78,100/year (expected). $78,100 in new costs. 3-year cumulative: $-234,300.
scenarioModeler.finding: Three-year projections with uncertainty ranges and a confidence badge, built on expense figures that are the budget column copied. The confidence is asserted about a simulation whose baseline was never measured.

verbatim: Note: Expense figures are estimated (94% FY elapsed). No actual expenditure data is currently available.
Budget pace: 94% spent at 94% of fiscal year (+0% vs expected).
Estimated idle fuel cost: $0/month across 81 vehicles.
Development Services: 397 permits issued ($0 in fees collected, $0 estimated construction value) - Full FY (MyGov).
findings: Budget pace of +0% against expected is an artefact, not a result. Spent equals budget by construction and elapsed drives the expectation, so the two track each other necessarily and the variance is always zero.
$0/month idle fuel across 81 vehicles is a fabricated zero presented as a measurement.
Development Services shows $0 fees collected on the same product where Permit Revenue shows Building Department collecting $243M. Two regions of one lens disagree.

v2Skeleton.ledeVerbatim: No metric strip on this lens. Four zeros in a header would be four false claims.
v2Skeleton.emptyVerbatim: This lens reads from the city's adopted budget, its fund ledger, permit fee revenue, and department spend. None of the four has been connected as a confirmed ledger, so there is nothing to report. That is not a zero balance.

v2Skeleton.note: The v2 register's four required sources map onto the capture exactly. v1 genuinely reads one of them, corrupts one, and fabricates two. That correspondence is what makes the gap analysis a design rather than a critique.
